The Petitioner had filed the Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act initially seeking Compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 30.06.2021.
However, during the trial the petitioner passed away and the Lrs have come on record.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 30.06.2021 at about 07.30 p.m., after work when he was returning home on the way to Ramanathapuram from Bettadapura Main Road, near K.Hosahalli New extension, infront of Kalyanamantapa Road, on the left side of the footpath, the 2nd respondent came on the bike bearing No.KA- 45-R-6740 with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner from behind.
Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on his different parts of the body.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to SCCH-25 HIMS Govt. Hospital wherein he has undergone treatment.
The MLC was immediately sent to the jurisdictional police but the police have not taken any action.
The wife of the petitioner has lodged the complaint against the offending vehicle on 07.07.2021 but by oversight mentioned the date as 01.07.2021 instead of 30.06.2021.
However, the accident occurred on 30.06.2021 and the same is recorded in the medical record also.
The petitioner was hale and healthy before the accident, working as a Coolie, earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
After the accident he was unable to work and had taken 6 months bed rest.

sentences.text: the Lrs of the petitioner averred that the death was due to the injuries suffered in accident and the amended petition is also filed.
The Konanur Police has registered a case against the rider of the motorcycle in Cr. No.199/2021 for the offences punishable u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The first respondent being the insurer and the 2nd respondent being SCCH-25 the RC owner cum rider of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
4. In response to the notice issued by this court, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
5. The objections of the respondent No1.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the vehicle bearing No.KA-45-R-6740 but, has stated that there is a delay in lodging the complaint, the delay was not properly explained.
The rider of the motorcycle did not have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
The petition is not maintainable for non compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134(c) of MV Act.
It has denied all the petition averments and prays for dismissal of the petition.

The respondent No.1 has also filed an additional written statement stating that the death of the petitioner occurred after lapse of 2 and half years from the date of accident and is not related to the injuries suffered in the accident.
This SCCH-25 relationship is not mentioned in the out patient record and the petitioners have not conducted the Post Mortem on the death of the petitioner.

Hence prays for dismissal of the petition.
6.
The objections of the respondent No2.
He has denied all the petition averments except accepting his ownership of the offending vehicle and that the respondent No.1 has issued policy in his favour.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed :
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident took place on 30.06.2021 at about 7.30pm near Bettadapura Main Road, near K.Hosahalli new Extension, infront of Kalyana Mantapa Road, due to rash and negligent act of riding of rider of Bike bearing Reg.No.KA- 45-R-6740 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries and due to the said injuries the petitioner died on 03.11.2023?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom ?
3. What order or award ?

My findings to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2 : In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per final order for the Following:-
REASONS
11 . Issue No.1:-
In order to prove that there was actionable negligence by the rider of the Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-45-R-6740, the SCCH-25 petitioner has originally examined as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 7.
During his cross examination he had stated that there was no continuous availability of labor to him.
He has admitted that he had taken treatment at Govt. Hospital.
He has also admitted that the accident occurred on a footpath which was about 2 feet above the Road.

He has admitted that he had the Mani vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167160684/

sentences.text: In support of their case the petitioner had examined the MRO at HIMS hospital as PW.2 and got marked marked Exs.P.20 to 23 authorization letter, MLC register extract, inpatient case sheet and eight X-rays.
The Investigation officer was also examined by the petitioner as PW.3 who has stated that even though he has received the police intimation he had not registered the FIR there.

During his cross examination by the counsel for the petitioner he has stated that as per the wound certificate at Ex.P.3 the date of accident was 30.06.2021 and even though the date was mentioned as 01.07.2021 in the complaint, by oversight he has mentioned the date of accident as 01.07.2021 even in the SCCH-25 charge sheet.

He has also admitted that the accident has occurred on the footpath as per the sketch at Ex.P.5.
12.

In order to prove the nexus between the death and injuries suffered by the petitioner during the accident, the wife of the petitioner got examined herself as PW.5 and got marked Exs.P.26 to 29 death certificate of petitioner, Aadhar cards of the Lrs of the petitioner, medical bills and 3 photos.
During her cross-examination she has admitted that she has not conducted any post mortum of petitioner.

On the other side, the Respondents have denied that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle and also stated that the death was not due to injuries suffered by the petitioner.
In order to prove the same the Respondent No.1 has examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 and 2 authorization letter and insurance policy.
During his cross-examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.
SCCH-25 13
. On perusal of the documents at Ex.P.1 it appears that the date of accident is 01.07.2021 and the FIR is registered on 07.07.2021.
In the complaint given at Ex.P.2 the date of accident is shown as 01.07.2021.
But in the wound certificate at Ex.P.3 the date of accident is shown as 30.06.2021.
The spot mahazar and spot sketch shows that the date of accident was 01.07.2021.
The spot sketch at Ex.P.5 shows that the accident occurred on the footpath.
As per Ex.P.6 MVA report the offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-45-R-6740 damaged to its front wheel mudguard, head lamp assembly and doumb cover damaged.
The police has filed charge sheet at Ex.P.7 against the rider of the motorcycle.
Therefore, on overall perusal of documents it appears that the is clear that the accident occurred on the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle since the spot of accident is a footpath.
14. There is a dispute about the date of the accident.
However, the date which is mentioned in the medical records is to be considered as those are the documents in first point SCCH-25 of time.
As per the petition the date of accident 30.06.2021 and not 01.07.2021 as shown in the police records.

The respondent has also contended that the petitioner had also filed an MVC 1383/2021 in a Hassan court, but the petitioner has filed Ex.P.12 a certified copy of the order sheet of the same case, which shows that the same was withdrawn by the petitioner by filing withdrawal memo.

Exs.P.13 to 15 i.e.,
the DL, RC and insurance policy show that the rider of the motorcycle had a valid and effective DL and there was a valid insurance to the vehicle as on the date of accident.
Therefore, on the basis of all the documents on record it is clear that the accident occurred due to the negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
During the pendency of the petition the deceased petitioner died on 03.11.2023 and his Lrs have come on record.

Therefore, the claimants are required to establish that due to actionable negligence on the part of the offending SCCH-25 vehicle the deceased petitioner sustained grievous injuries and there is also nexus between the death of Mani and the injures suffered by him in the accident.

16. In order to prove that due to injuries suffered in the accident the petitioner died, the Lrs of petitioner have neither produced the postmortem examination nor the inquest mahazar of the deceased nor the medical documents pertaining to the deceased nor the second FIS nor additional chargesheet to support their claim.

The counsel for the Respondent No.1 has relied upon a citation as under:
Civil Appeal No.1638/2010 : Rasheeda Haroon Kupurade Vs. Div. Manager, Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., & Ors.

17. The petitioners have only produced chargesheet, FIR, FIS, spot mahazar, spot sketch, wound certificate, MVA report and death certificate as per Exs.P.1 to 7 and P.26.

As per these documents,
the accident occurred on 01.07.2021, whereas the deceased died on 03.11.2023 i.e., almost after the lapse of Two years Four months from the date of accident.

Ex. P.8/discharge summary of Hims Hospital, Hassan, clearly shows that the petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 01.07.2021 with alleged history of RTA on 30.06.2021 at around 8.00 p.m. at Hassan and discharged on 10.07.2021 and diagnosed fracture of left clavicle, left IT fracture of femur, fracture of BB type IIIb, left leg distal 1/3rd and from SCCH-25 this it is clear that because of injuries suffered in the accident, he has taken treatment in the above said hospital.

sentences.text: Out of these injuries, injury No.1 and 5 are grievous in nature and 2, 3 and 4 are simple in nature.

But the petitioners have not produced any documents to prove that as to what kind of treatment was provided to the petitioner after discharge on 10.07.2021 till the date of death and hence it can be inferred that no treatment was provided to the petitioner.
During the cross of PW.1 it is brought out by the counsel for the Respondent No.1 that the they have not conducted any post mortum of the petitioner.
They have not filed any report from any medical officer showing the reason for death of petitioner.

SCCH-25 Ex.P.1 clearly shows that the chargesheet filed on 01.07.2021 is for the offences u/Sec.279,
337 of IPC only showing grievous injury to the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioners have not led any evidence to prove that the deceased died on account of injuries sustained in the accident.
In support of his case, the counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the decision in Civil Appeal No.4800/2021 dated 16.08.2021: The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon.

entities.text: Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has considered the decisions of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Kanamma and Uttam Kumar case and has held that the insurance company cannot evade from its obligation by hiding behind the defence that the death is attributable to the reasons other than the accident.

It is further held that loss of estate would include expenditure on medical expenses, traveling, attendant, diet, doctors fee and reasonable monthly annual accretion to the estate for a certain period.
The court goes on to explain that Loss of Estate is the income and future prospects.
SCCH-25 18

. The Petitioners have stated that they have spent huge amount towards medical, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges etc..
In this regard they have produced medical bills and prescriptions as per Exs.P.17, 18 and 28 for Rs.2,830/- + Rs.6,119/-, in total Rs.8,949/-.
There is no contrary evidence to these documents.
As such, the petitioners are entitled for total amount of Rs.8,949/- under the head of medical expenses.
During the time of treatment, certainly the petitioner might have spent some amount towards conveyance, transportation and for other incidental expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards conveyance, transportation, food, nourishment and other incidental expenses.
Income and future prospects:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as a Mason and doing Milk business and earning Rs.20,000/-.
The same contention is repeated by his Lrs.

However,
neither the petitioner nor PW.5 has produced any documents to show his income or avocation.
The notional SCCH-25 income for the year 2021 is at Rs.15,000/- per month and the Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/- per month.
As per Aadhar Card of the petitioner at Ex.P.9 the petitioner was aged about 37 years as on the date of accident.
As per Sarala Verma's case the multiplier applicable is 15.

The deceased petitioner comes under the slab of below Mani vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167160684/
7 40 years, so 40% future prospectus should be added to the income.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Then the income comes to Rs.21,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 40% = Rs.6,000/-).
The wife and a minor son have come on record as Lrs of the petitioner after his death.
Both are dependants of the deceased.
Therefore, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Therefore, his monthly income comes to Rs.14,000/- (Rs.21,000/- - Rs.7,000/- =Rs.14,000).
The Lrs of the deceased are entitled to Rs.25,20,000/- (Rs.14,000/- x 12 x 15) under the head of Income and future prospects.
In total, the compensation comes to Rs.25,58,949/- and if it is rounded off it comes to Rs.25,59,000/-.
SCCH-25 LIABILITY:-

19. This court while considering the Issue No.1 has already come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-45-R-6740.
The respondents have not proved their defence by leading cogent evidence.
Therefore, the LRs of the deceased Petitioner are entitled for above compensation from the Respondents.
Though the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- but they are only entitled for compensation of Rs.25,59,000/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum.
The Respondents 1 and 2 being the Insurer and the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Lrs of the deceased petitioner.
However, as the policy existed, the respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to indemnify the insured respondent No.2 and to deposit the compensation awarded to the petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
SCCH-25 20. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and findings to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed u/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed with cost.

The legal Representatives of the deceased petitioner are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,59,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Fifty Nine Thousand only) from the Respondents along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The respondent No.1/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest SCCH-25 before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this judgment.

Therefore, the claimants are required to establish that due to actionable negligence on the part of the offending SCCH-25 vehicle the deceased petitioner sustained grievous injuries and there is also nexus between the death of Mani and the injures suffered by him in the accident.
16. In order to prove that due to injuries suffered in the accident the petitioner died, the Lrs of petitioner have neither produced the postmortem examination nor the inquest mahazar of the deceased nor the medical documents pertaining to the deceased nor the second FIS nor additional chargesheet to support their claim.
The counsel for the Respondent No.1 has relied upon a citation as under:
Civil Appeal No.1638/2010 : Rasheeda Haroon Kupurade Vs. Div. Manager, Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., & Ors.
Therefore, the petitioners have not led any evidence to prove that the deceased died on account of injuries sustained in the accident.
As such, the petitioners are entitled for total amount of Rs.8,949/- under the head of medical expenses.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the LRs of the deceased Petitioner are entitled for above compensation from the Respondents.
Though the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- but they are only entitled for compensation of Rs.25,59,000/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum.
The Respondents 1 and 2 being the Insurer and the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Lrs of the deceased petitioner.
However, as the policy existed, the respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to indemnify the insured respondent No.2 and to deposit the compensation awarded to the petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
SCCH-25 20. Issue No.3:-
For the reasons and discussions made above and findings to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed u/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed with cost.
The legal Representatives of the deceased petitioner are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,59,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Fifty Nine Thousand only) from the Respondents along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The respondent No.1/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest SCCH-25 before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this judgment.
Mani vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167160684/
8
On deposit of compensation and interest, Rs.10,00,000/- shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner Lr (b) till he attains the age of majority in any N/S Bank and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner Lr (a) through e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
